assertions: Exact start state and five enemy slots, submitted command actor/target/order and completed action before/after state.
One/three distinct HP30 lanterns receive the selected lethal ordinary attacks, with no undeclared autonomous enemy action.
Herb99 heals hero50 to100 and consumes exactly one of two; formal victory yields hero125, exp1 and cash3. Party victory gives each member exp3 and cash9.
Formal settlement commits exactly once; all three cases pass independent state oracles, cross-engine effective-state comparison and same-engine native/rule-RNG repeat checks.

A real isolated double-consumption mutant fails business/action-after at actions[0].after with inventory2 tozero; restoring normal serve mode passes. Missing hashes, input receipts and fresh contexts are rejected by the offline entry.

Real rendered frames show the manual selection HUD, hide it during action and settlement, finish each enemy fade before the next action, and draw herb50 on the returned actor with the original recipient anchor.
The fixed ordinary attack cases check CLASSIC draw purposes, queue jitter, untruncated attack numbers and clamped enemy HP. Actual draws are logged at their producers.
The two-round case checks guard, real enemy damage, a single herb consumption, cancellation and same-actor retarget, heal296 MP and recipient HP, and single settlement.
Team294 consumes no singleton target draw. Native dual actions use 339 for HP94 then normal attack for HP44, with separate raw and rendered results.
Team204 consumes the native battle script chance draw. Sleep3 applies to hero, round ends tick 3→2→1, and the incapacitated slot passes without a submitted action.
Team115 passes the equivalent-item and 0x29 resistance rolls. Direct blue1 is separate from immediate poison HP7 and round-end HP7. Item87 consumes one and cures 551 before the next round.

The actual Li Xiaoyao portrait shows the original RGBA values before poison and after item87, and exact SDLPal palette-ramp RGBs while poison551 is active. Two transparent pixels preserve their drawn destination.
In team115, first actual round-end blue7 precedes the next selection HUD by the original eight-tick feedback hold. The cured round has no new number and opens selection on normal scheduling.

After the first native command, each of the 45 finite expected action cues has one real connected AudioBufferSourceNode start on a running context and the matching nonzero decoded WAV. Request order, repeated cue identity, actual action windows, enemy windup and enemy fade edges are checked.
In seed72, the first drawn impact and recoil use frame4. The first actual return and the remaining turn1 recovery use frame3, then the round-end poison number appears in idle frame0.

In seed11, the first drawn enemy charge already shows player frame3 and retains that pose through knockback. Recovery returns to the original idle frame. HP is unchanged, no damage number is drawn, and the actual strike cue starts the player cover WAV 015.

In seed72, the native active-defend commit, executed guard action, first drawn defense, first drawn enemy windup and first blue physical damage occur in that order. The two one-tick intervals must each lie in 20–65 ms; the attack-to-damage interval is 280–360 ms. Two native cross-engine pairs also verify a command-to-windup difference within one CLASSIC tick.

The lantern hits Li for 35 then 5. The actual impact frame 4 and two recoil positions precede first return frames 1 and 2. Native sound 019 starts after the dying pose; 023 starts around second recoil and before the fallen pose. Each appears once and the regular hit sound 352 still starts at each impact.

After lethal damage the native equivalent-item roll is consumed, with zero rate. Li’s selected action is skipped and Anu’s real 976 raw damage wins. The original victory reward leaves Li with zero earned EXP and 20 HP after half recovery, Anu with one EXP and 150 HP, and awards cash 3 once.

The two casualty branches keep their actual portrait frames, automatic pages and narration. The guardian heals and gains the temporary attack bonus only after the dialogue clears, before his own strike.
Enemy thunder consumes the same probability stream, drops Li from 85 to 27 or from 24 to zero, draws five impact beats and returns to the correct final pose with the respective actual native sound.
Turn-end poison numbers start from the returned position. The pre-poison pose persists eight beats before dying or falling, with no extra casualty cue or dialogue in these poison cases.

Ordinary defeat retains the last battle background across the red palette progression. The original death music starts, the game-over text waits for a real confirmation, black renders before the real restore, and fixed m01 returns the party to the dock with 1 HP.

Five matching single-enemy damages and MP costs. Wind seed6 draws enemy variance then cast growth, gives 82 damage and 3 hidden MP growth. Area skills draw once per enemy slot before growth; lethal damage numbers retain the full formula result.

Successful co-op pays 10 HP per healthy contributor, consumes the partner action, does 161 damage and no MP spend. The contributor HP cost changes battle state without player damage digits. Wood sword uses bare attack to do 219, spends one bag item and plays windup followed by its spell effect. The actual damage draw precedes four battle frames in release and four after returning, then the queue resumes.

Enemy target cancellation precedes native submission. Player sleep uses chance and target resistance before growth. The affected enemy actually passes and duration decrements even in a retained defeated slot. Resistance draws the original notice before the next action.

Protect applies for 7 turns, decrements to 6, halves the two fixed physical hits, and clears at victory. The cleanse control does not apply the buff. In both single-ally cases the rendered FIRE sequence is anchored to and painted in front of the selected ally, followed by that ally’s original glow.

Spell paint probes bind the original signed layer and byte-identical FIRE resource. Native draws must use that FIRE chunk, cover its source frames and paint in the original order against the relevant live fighters. The exact 381 position is (98,100) against enemy slot 0 at (100,110).

A cooperative submission that loses its only teammate executes a normal equipped attack. Each native hit, actual swing at the number birth, stable target anchor, per-hit sound, HP delta and RNG sequence is checked. No cooperative HP or MP cost.

Ordinary offensive spells retain the advanced cast pose through the original nine-tick recovery. Damage numbers appear within the first actual reaction pose, stable after return, then the same next actor starts. The two measured windows are cross-engine bounded.

Item settlement checks the same native command and target, one inventory deduction, each raw damage or restoration, effective HP and MP, poison changes, exact rule RNG order, and ordinary settlement. Throw numbers use the per-target signed raw change, including overkill and mixed throw steps.

Numbers and animation come from observed frames. Check whole-party glow, actual FIRE frames and paint order, same-frame drain damage and recovery at the acting foot, recovery pose on revival, and timing from raise through the first number to the next actor.
A queued attack after sleep cleanse must come from the expected native player slot after another actor uses Lingxin Talisman, with no submitted attack in that round.
Party healing draws FIRE28 once at each live actor anchor, with all declared recipients present and original paint order. Drain preserves the captured entry pose in all four approach steps.

A salt throw consumes one item, draws raise and release without effect feedback, and emits the throw cue without a rule draw. The following equipped double strike preserves both hits and their RNG on the same enemy slot after lethal damage.

Enemy casts must visibly approach in two PAL ticks, preserve their advanced position through actual FIRE frames, animate the correct delayed pose, show guard and net HP feedback at the intended boundaries, and return after five reaction ticks.

Real poison item commands verify six directed cures, three lethal pairs in both orders by use and throw, resistance and precedence, the first player/enemy poison entry, Dragon Gall and Shadowless Poison. Focused HP, poisons, RNG values and native number draws agree directly across engines.

Text in all seven paired native settlement screens agrees with the original bitmaps and PAL palette for glyph shape, adjacency inside each label, color and lack of text shadow. The separate Reforge main-menu cash label matches the original 0 color and no shadow.
